item.title: China International Talent Exchange Foundation CEP Program Kick-off Meeting
item.description:
The China International Talent Exchange Foundation CEP Program was officially launched. The kick-off meeting for the “2026 Green Energy Materials and Devices Thermal Management International Internship Program” was held at Yangtze Delta Region Academy in Jiaxing, Beijing Institute of Technology, with participants including institute leaders, researchers, and internship students from Universiti Malaya (QS 56). The program aims to deepen international scientific cooperation, strengthen youth talent cultivation, and promote exchanges between BIT and Universiti Malaya in research collaboration, joint postgraduate training, and youth talent exchange, with a focus on green energy, advanced materials, and sustainable development, while supporting China-ASEAN cooperation and the Belt and Road Initiative.

Link: https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/8NrXH3dfAHOye1CfLSEAng

item.title: Visited to Monash University Malaysia
item.description:
In September 2026, I visited the Micro/Nanoscale Heat Transfer Laboratory at Monash University Malaysia for academic exchange. During the visit, I delivered a seminar on “Molecular Dynamics Study on Nano/Microscale Thermal Energy Transport” and shared our recent work on thermal transport across nanoscale systems and interfaces. The discussion with faculty members and researchers covered molecular dynamics simulations, interfacial heat transfer, and related micro/nanoscale thermal management topics. This visit also provided a good opportunity to explore common research interests and possible directions for future collaboration between our teams.

Link: https://www.monash.edu.my/engineering/all-disciplines/mechanical-engineering/our-research_3/thermofluidics/micronanoscale-heat-transfer-research-team

item.title: Visited to Polytechnic University of Turin
item.description:
In June 2026, I had the pleasure of visiting the Multi-Scale Modeling Laboratory at Polytechnic University of Turin, Italy. During the visit, I had valuable academic discussions with Prof. Eliodoro Chiavazzo and Prof. Matteo Fasano on multiscale modeling, micro/nanoscale heat transfer, and interfacial thermal transport. The visit provided an excellent opportunity to learn about the recent research activities of the SMaLL Lab and to exchange ideas on potential future collaborations. It was an inspiring and rewarding academic exchange, and I look forward to further communication and collaboration in the future.

Link: https://small.polito.it/index.html

item.title: Establishment Meeting of Micro-Nano System Thermal Management Branch, Chinese Society of Micro-Nano Technology
item.description:
On January 31, 2026, the establishment meeting of Micro-Nano System Thermal Management Branch of the Chinese Society of Micro-Nano Technology, along with the first session of its inaugural committee, was successfully convened at Tsinghua University in Beijing. Over fifty leading scholars and representatives in micro-nano thermal management from universities and research institutions across the nation gathered to witness this significant milestone. The establishment of this branch signifies Chinese creation of a dedicated academic community and collaborative innovation platform in the critical frontier field of micro-nano system thermal management.

Link: https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/YruAn4xHneq7tX5pl2svMw?click_id=10

item.title: Visited to University of Ulsan
item.description:
In September 2025, I had the pleasure of visiting Prof. BoHung Kim’s group at the University of Ulsan, South Korea. Prof. Kim kindly delivered a seminar introducing his group’s recent research progress, followed by a tour of the laboratory and the Ulsan campus. The visit also provided valuable opportunities for open and friendly discussions with Korean students and international graduate students. It was an inspiring and rewarding academic exchange, and I look forward to potential future collaborations.

Link: https://sites.google.com/site/bohungkim/home

item.title: International Forum for Excellent Young Scholars
item.description:
I was honored to be invited to the International Forum for Excellent Young Scholars at Chongqing University on June, 2025. item.title: JST NEXUS Exchange Program
item.description:
📢We are excited to share highlights from our recent visit to UMPEDAC Universiti Malaya! From March 8th to 13th, our Kyutech Heat Transfer Lab group had the incredible opportunity to collaborate and exchange knowledge, all thanks to the support of the JST NEXUS project.🌸

During our visit, we engaged in sharing our latest findings and exploring cutting-edge advancements in heat transfer, experiencing the impressive facilities and vibrant academic environment at UMPEDAC, and brainstorming and planning future research collaborations, fostering strong ties between our institutions.

We’re immensely grateful to UMPEDAC for their warm hospitality and for facilitating such a productive exchange. This collaboration is a significant step towards advancing our research and strengthening international partnerships.

item.title: Japan-Asia Youth Exchange Program in Science
item.description:
From October 2024 to January 2025, Kyutech organized an online international exchange program titled “Global Engineering Education in Mechanical Engineering Field through Online Project Based Learning.” This initiative was part of the Sakura Science Plan, supported by Japan Science and Technology Agency (JST).

The program attracted 47 participants, comprising 36 students and 11 faculty members from institutions including Qingdao University of Technology, Northeastern University (CN), Shandong University, University of Malaya, National Taiwan University of Science and Technology, Yanshan University, Qilu University of Technology, Indian Institute of Technology, Guwahati, and University of Southern California.

International Joint Seminar on Mechanical Engineering 2024 was held to promote academic exchange in mechanical engineering field. The participants enjoyed 6 keynote lectures and 42 oral presentations through Zoom. Online events such as campus/laboratory tours, and collaborative works have been conducted by 36 foreign students together with 21 Japanese students. All participants worked diligently with their teams to complete the projects “Spin” and “Magnetic” successfully. This online event fostered international cooperation and strengthened friendships among all involved.

This program was supported by JST.

Link: https://www.kyutech.ac.jp/english/en-news/topics/entry-11151.html

item.title: Served as session chairman at SAES2024
item.description:
Thrilled to share that I had the honor of chairing a session on Engineering & Technology at the 12th International Symposium on Applied Engineering and Sciences (SAES2024), held at the Faculty of Engineering, Kyushu Institute of Technology!

SAES2024 is an international forum for presentations and interactions in the current and emerging areas of Applied Engineering and Sciences. It also provides a unique platform for researchers, students, scientist and engineers to share their experiences and views of their latest research breakthrough.

Grateful for the opportunity to be part of such an inspiring event and to witness the exciting research shaping the future of technology. Looking forward to seeing how these discussions will continue to drive innovation and collaboration in the years to come!

Link: https://conferenceservice.jp/www/saes2024/

item.title: Japan-Asia Youth Exchange Program in Science
item.description:
Kyutech held an international exchange program “Enhancement of International Exchange Partnerships and Global Engineering Education in Mechanical Engineering Field” under SAKURA Science Exchange Program sponsored by JST from June 9 to 14, 2024 at Tobata campus.

10 participants including 7 students and 3 faculty members from Qingdao University of Technology, Northeastern University (CN), Qilu University of Technology and Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati were invited to join this program.

International Joint Seminar on Mechanical Engineering 2024 took place to enhance academic exchange in mechanical engineering field. The participants enjoyed the 4 keynote lectures, 8 oral presentations. Events such as campus/laboratory tours and collaborative works have been conducted by 7 foreign students together with 22 Japanese students. This event prometed the international exchange and friendship of all the participants.

This program was supported by JST, Kitakyushu City and Kitakyushu Convention and Visitors Association.

Link: https://www.kyutech.ac.jp/english/en-news/topics/entry-10692.html

item.title: Visited to University of Malaya
item.description:
I am thrilled to share the incredible experiences I’ve had during my recent visit to UMPEDAC Universiti Malaya on November, 2023. The warmth and hospitality extended by the faculty and students have truly left an indelible mark on my journey.

It was an honor to introduce Kyushu Institute of Technology (Kyutech) and our Heat Transfer Lab to the esteemed members of UMPADEC. The potential for future collaborations between our institutions is a source of great excitement, and I am eager to explore the possibilities that lie ahead.

My sincere appreciation goes to the UMPADEC team for guiding me through enlightening visits to the Solar Cell Lab, Hydrogen Lab, PVT Thermal Lab, and the Solar Garden. These experiences have not only expanded my knowledge but also enriched my research insights, providing valuable perspectives that will undoubtedly contribute to our shared academic pursuits.

Engaging in discussions with University of Malaya students has been a highlight of my visit. The enthusiasm and passion exhibited by the students are truly commendable, and I look forward to the prospect of continued exchange programs between our faculties and students. To the talented UM students, I extend a warm invitation to consider the opportunities for study at Kyutech.

I express my heartfelt gratitude for the efforts put forth by the UMPADEC team in facilitating these experiences. Your warm welcome and support have made my visit exceptionally memorable. I am confident that these interactions have laid the foundation for strong bonds between our institutions.

We eagerly anticipate further interactions and collaborations that will undoubtedly strengthen the ties between the Kyushu Institute of Technology and the University of Malaya. Together, we can propel academic excellence and innovation to new heights.

item.title: Japan-Asia Youth Exchange Program in Science
item.description:
An online exchange program has been held by Heat Transfer Laboratory, Department of Mechanical Engineering at Kyushu Institute of Technology under SAKURA Exchange Program in Science by Japan Science and Technology Agency (JST) from Oct. 6 2023 to Feb. 2 2024.

A total of 38 participants who were invited to this online exchange program are from Free University of Bozen-Bolzano, National Taiwan University of Science and Technology, Nanyang Technological University Singapore, University of Ulsan, Qingdao University of Technology, Northeastern University (CN), Shandong University, and Qilu University of Technology. They positively gave presentations at International Joint Seminar on Mechanical Engineering 2022, joined online laboratory tours, and finished collaborative works by making spins and windmills with Japanese students.

This online event enhanced the international exchange among all the participants. Kyutech will keep the relationship with its partner universities for education development.

Link: https://www.kyutech.ac.jp/whats-new/topics/entry-9643.html
